title: Senior Backend Engineer (TypeScript / Nest.js / AWS)
description:
Employment type: FULL_TIME
Applicants must be located in: Poland
Full-time B2B | Remote EU / Poland | US Insurance Context | Start October 2026We are an AI-native data and technology partner for private capital and healthcare. Founded in 2010 and headquartered in Warsaw, we work with leading PE firms, VC funds, and healthcare organizations to build proprietary data infrastructure, deploy AI solutions, and drive AI-native transformation.Our clients manage a cumulative $1.2T+ in assets. Our average engagement runs five years. Our NPS sits above 80. We don't need to claim credibility - we can show it.We've also done to ourselves what we now do for clients. We've restructured our own company around AI - tools, policies, roles, delivery models. This isn't a pitch. It's a playbook we've already run, and we're hiring the engineers who will run it for others.The OpportunityOur client is a US insurance carrier building a platform business on top of its own paper: a set of operational services it offers to the specialist insurers (MGAs) it underwrites for. The first service is claims - the carrier is becoming the claims administrator for its partners, running their claims in a shared instance of a modern claims platform. That platform only knows how to talk to one policy system, and every partner has their own. The missing piece is a multi-tenant policy gateway, and it is the blocking dependency for the first partner's go-live at the start of 2027.You'll be the engineer who builds it. You'll work in a small pod with our tech lead and directly with the client's staff engineer, engineering manager and claims domain expert, in their codebase and on their AWS. We already run the data platform for the client's first partner, so you join a team that knows both ends of the integration. The environment is fast-moving and the spec is a PRD, not a design - we're expected to propose, decide and deliver, not wait for tickets.What you'll be doingThe core of the work is a greenfield Nest.js / TypeScript service that sits between the claims platform and N external policy systems: it authenticates the incoming webhook, resolves which tenant a request belongs to, fetches the policy (live API call or from a policy store fed by daily file extracts), maps it through a canonical policy model and returns it in the claims platform's schema - with hard data isolation between tenants, because a misrouted policy is a cross-tenant data leak. Around that core you'll define the canonical model, drive the first partner's field-mapping through business review, build the observability and the onboarding runbook that turns tenant #2 into a configuration exercise, and take the whole thing through security review and launch readiness. Expect to spend real time reading the client's existing single-tenant precedent and their internal framework conventions before you write your own.Your ResponsibilitiesDesign and build the gateway service on the client's Nest.js-based internal framework and AWS, proposing infrastructure changes as Terraform PRs for their DevOps team to applyImplement the webhook contract: HMAC authentication in application code with secrets in Vault, IP allowlisting, ISO-8601 date handling, policy-version-at-date-of-loss selectionBuild the tenant router and registry with composite resolution and well-defined failure behaviourBuild the source adapter framework - a common interface with per-source auth, timeouts, retries with backoff and circuit breaking so one slow tenant source cannot degrade the webhook for othersBuild the batch path: SFTP landing zones per tenant, file validation and quarantine, idempotent loads into a PostgreSQL policy store with snapshot retention and freshness monitoringDefine the canonical policy model and the shared canonical-to-target mapper; take the first partner's mapping tables (coverage codes, deductible types, roles) through review with the client's claims expertShip per-tenant observability (structured logs, metrics, Grafana dashboard, freshness and error-rate alerts) and an onboarding runbookWrite isolation negative tests as a release gate, run failure-mode drills and end-to-end walkthroughs in the client's sandbox, and support their security reviewCollaborate directly with client engineers and domain experts across time zones, largely async. Some availability in PT timezone would be required - not more than once a week.Required Skills & Experience5+ years backend engineering with strong, recent TypeScript in production; Nest.js or a comparable DI-based Node frameworkExperience building integration services or API gateways: webhooks, signature-based auth, retries, idempotency, circuit breakers, third-party API adaptersPostgreSQL and relational data modelling; comfortable designing schemas and writing migrationsExperience with multi-tenant systems or another domain where data isolation is a hard requirement, and the instinct to test it explicitlyHands-on AWS (ECS/EKS or Lambda, SQS, S3, IAM, Secrets Manager or Vault); able to read and propose Terraform even if someone else applies itAI-native way of working: you use tools like Claude Code and Codex as a core part of how you deliver, and you still read every line that shipsSelf-directed: able to scope ambiguous requests, write a short design note, ask the client the right question early, and deliver without heavy oversightFluent English and clear, proactive communication with technical and non-technical stakeholdersNice to HaveInsurance domain exposure - policy administration systems, claims, FNOL, coverages and deductibles, MGA/carrier structuresBatch or file-based integrations (SFTP ingestion, schema validation, quarantine patterns) or data-mapping heavy workRegulated-data experience: PII/PHI handling, HIPAA or SOC 2 controls, audit loggingGrafana / OpenTelemetry-style observabilityPrior consulting or client-facing deliveryBene

Feed the product. Custom agents you write get contributed back. Integration patterns get codified. Production bugs you find, you often fix. Your field work is a direct input to ProcessOS.

We're hiring a Senior Software Engineer . Not a senior title for someone who executes well, but the engineer other engineers calibrate against. You see the thing that's broken, decide it's worth fixing, and start. Nobody assigns that to you.

We want to be blunt about the bar, because last time we weren't. This role is not "ship tickets faster than a mid-level engineer". It's technical leadership, coaching, challenging how we work, and being the person the EM and PM think out loud with. If that's not the job you want, this will be a bad year for both of us.

About Workwize

Workwize is the platform IT teams use to equip and manage remote and global workforces. We deliver, track, and retrieve hardware in over 100 countries, with 50,000 users and 120,000 devices under management today.

We're one of the fastest-growing scale-ups in the Netherlands, a LinkedIn Top 10 Startup (2025) and ranked #6 by Deloitte in the 50 fastest-growing Dutch tech companies. We work from a flat, open environment out of our Amsterdam HQ and across 40+ nationalities worldwide.

What you'll do

Lead feature work end to end: shape the scope with the PM, make the architectural calls, decide what to cut, and own whether it actually worked once it's live.

Use agents and AI tooling as your default way of building, and pull the rest of the team up to where you are. What you can do with a model this month should be what the team can do with it next month.

Coach the engineers around you, including the ones who are not junior. Pairing, review, handing over scope, and direct feedback that changes how someone works.

Change how we work without asking permission first. Spot the process that's costing the team time, build the case, get the buy in, and show the before and after.

Be a real partner to the EM and PM. Push back on the roadmap, bring the problem nobody had noticed, and say the uncomfortable thing early rather than politely late.

Connect what you ship to what the company is trying to achieve, with a number you chose and then went back and looked at.

Who you are

You have 8+ years building software at product companies, and you're currently a Senior Software Engineer, Lead Engineer, Tech Lead, Senior Full Stack Engineer, Senior Product Engineer or similar. You've worked in a real cross functional team, not alone and not in a two person shop.

You have a deep technical and architecture foundation. You can explain how the systems you built fit together, why you made each trade off, and what would break first under load. AI makes you faster, it does not stand in for understanding what you shipped.

You use AI and agents as your default way of working, and you can name the tools, models and harnesses. You know exactly which parts you still do yourself and why, and you read what the agent produced closely wherever it touches data, money or auth.

You've coached peers, not only juniors, and you can point to a specific skill someone has now because of you.

You've driven a change in how a team works and confirmed with a metric that it landed.

You're an extremely strong communicator. You get to the point, you can hold a constructive disagreement without it getting personal, and feedback is something you go looking for rather than something you survive.

You have judgment about what not to build. The fastest way to ship is to cut the right thing, and you'll defend that call.

You're proactive to the point of being slightly annoying about it. You'd rather fix it and tell people afterwards than raise it and wait.

Nice to have

Experience at a fast growing SaaS or B2B product company.

Running evals, watching inference cost, or dealing with model failure modes like hallucination in production.

Experience being the technical counterpart for a PM or EM on a roadmap, not just on a sprint.

What this role is not

Not a role where improvements wait for a one on one. If you need to be asked, this isn't it.

Not a role where seniority means scope of tickets. It means scope of influence.

Not a role where you can be excellent alone. If the team isn't better a quarter after you join, we both got it wrong.
